subject: crtf-d
title: CRTF.D.------ALT.F.
description: Diagram in CMOA(II)-34 (Creative Music Outside of America, Level One — France/Italy/Northern Europe/Japan), first of two on book p276. Sits within Braxton's Japan analysis, after his statement that 'the present reality of Japanese creativity is not available for international scrutiny.' (C)CRTF-D (the concept of cross-transfer definitions) is crossed with ALT-F (alternative functionalism): the question is what cross-transfer-definitions produces when crossed with alternative-functionalism under conditions of the Japan-West one-way culture gap. The main line runs from the subject down to ALT-F, which sits centrally below. PROG-CONT (progressional continuance) branches from the main line, and (P)CULT-INFO-DY (culture-information dynamics at its point of idea completion) branches from PROG-CONT to the upper right. Three lines leave the CULT-INFO-DY line: POL-DY (political dynamics) rises above it; PROJ-CONT (projectional continuance) and LK-IMP (linkage implications) share the end of a line on the right; and DYM-F (dynamic functionalism) drops below it, with INFO-DS (information dissemination) branching from DYM-F and STF (source transfer) from INFO-DS. Structural argument: cross-transfer-definitions-as-concept crossed with alternative-functionalism carries all of its side structure through progressional-continuance and culture-information-dynamics; ALT-F has no branches of its own.
